Abstract vs. Section 5.1 count mismatch: the Abstract cites '128-assignment WSAT checks' (the size of F4 alone), whereas Contributions and Section 5.1 report '224-assignment Lemma 4 sweeps' (16+16+64+128 = 224 across F1-F4).

summary: This 4-page manuscript presents a machine-checked Lean 4.35.0 formalization and exact-integer certificate auditor for the structural dichotomy, Edmonds matroid-intersection duality, shifted-weight telescoping, series-parallel WSAT semantics, Partitioned Subgraph Isomorphism 5|E(H)| tightness, and {1,1}-to-{2,1} K_{1,*} gadget invariants established by Kern, Firbas, and Sorge (arXiv:2611.32927). All mathematical invariants stated in Section 2 and combinatorial counts in Section 5 (such as the 41-graph 4-vertex census: 14+3+12+12) are sound, scope exclusions regarding NP/W[1]/ETH hardness and asymptotic runtime are transparently stated, and no material objections invalidate the main results, though the PDF omits the formal Lean type signatures and contains minor presentation inconsistencies.
weaknesses: The 4-page PDF lists theorem names and informal descriptions in Table 1 and Section 3 without displaying the actual Lean 4 definitions or theorem type signatures, preventing independent verification from the manuscript alone that the formalized abstractions (e.g., matroid rank or transition paths) faithfully match the graph-theoretic definitions in [3].

As explicitly noted by the author, the core complexity-theoretic hardness reductions (NP, W[1], W[SAT], ETH) and polynomial-time matroid-intersection algorithm are outside the Lean 4 formalization scope, leaving mainly structural, algebraic, and weak-duality invariants proved in Lean.
Empirical details for formulas F1-F4, the 16 canonical instances, and the 57 adversarial test vectors are summarized only at a high level in the PDF and require inspecting the external repository.
